<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
A prior specification exists for the API service project setup.

The API service will be a separate FastAPI project with a basic-authenticated UI. Upload sessions will handle leave and onsite data, requiring year and month inputs. The backend will create missing MinIO folders before storing entries. A sibling folder like `employee_upload_api/` is being considered for project placement.

HTTP Basic Auth will be used for browser-native authentication. MinIO credentials and application users will be loaded from environment variables. The service will store files directly without triggering DAGs. MinIO uses prefixes rather than traditional folders.

Uploads will target `.xlsx` files to match the existing pipeline. Missing MinIO prefixes will be created by uploading a placeholder object ending in `/` before storing the actual file. Existing ingest logic concatenates all `.xlsx` files within a month folder, so the service should overwrite or merge uploads accordingly.

Multiple files per month will be allowed, preserving original filenames to match the existing ingest glob pattern. DAG triggers are out of scope. Authentication will rely on a single shared credential set from environment variables.

A login form with session cookies is preferred over HTTP Basic Auth for a smoother user experience.

FastAPI HTTP Basic Auth will be used for both API endpoints and UI pages. This follows the standard web API interpretation of basic authentication.

The new project should be added to `.airflowignore` so Airflow does not pick it up. A single FastAPI project will serve HTML templates directly rather than using a separate frontend framework. A simple Dockerfile and `.env.example` will be included for local development. Uploaded Excel files should be validated against expected column headers to prevent invalid data from reaching MinIO.
</details></think>

{
  "name": "FastAPI Upload Service",
  "overview": "Add a new sibling FastAPI project with a login UI and two upload flows (leave and onsite). Files go to MinIO `lakehouse` under year/month folders matching the existing Spark ingest paths; missing month prefixes are created first.",
  "plan": "# FastAPI Leave/Onsite Upload Service\n\n## Context\n\nLeave and onsite Excel currently land in MinIO by hand (`mc cp`). Spark jobs already expect:\n\n- Bucket: `lakehouse`\n- Leave: `leave_employee/{YYYY}/{month}/` e.g. `leave_employee/2026/september/`\n- Onsite: `onsite_employee/{YYYY}/{month}/`\n- Month folders: **lowercase English names** (`january` … `december`), same as [`month_folder_name`](employee_data/dependencies/scripts/leave_data.py) in the ingest jobs\n- Files: `.xlsx` only; all workbooks in a month folder are concatenated on ingest\n\nThis service **only lands files in MinIO**. It will not trigger Airflow DAGs.\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  User --\u003e LoginUI\n  LoginUI --\u003e UploadUI\n  UploadUI --\u003e FastAPI\n  FastAPI --\u003e EnsurePrefix[\"Ensure YYYY/month prefix\"]\n  EnsurePrefix --\u003e MinIO[\"lakehouse bucket\"]\n```\n\n## Project location\n\nNew sibling directory: [`employee_upload_api/`](employee_upload_api/) next to `employee_data/` and `saal-data-model/`.\n\nAlso add `employee_upload_api/` to [`.airflowignore`](.airflowignore) so Airflow does not try to parse it as DAGs.\n\n```\nemployee_upload_api/\n  app/\n    main.py              # FastAPI app, static/templates, auth middleware\n    config.py            # pydantic-settings from env\n    auth.py              # login + session cookie\n    minio_service.py     # prefix check/create + put object\n    schemas.py           # upload dataset type, year, month\n    templates/\n      login.html\n      upload.html\n    static/\n      styles.css\n  tests/\n    test_auth.py\n    test_minio_service.py\n    test_upload_api.py\n  requirements.txt\n  .env.example\n  README.md\n```\n\n## UI and auth\n\n- Simple HTML UI served by FastAPI (Jinja2). No separate frontend app.\n- **Login page** with username and password. After success, a signed **session cookie** protects the upload page and API.\n- Credentials from env (`APP_USERNAME`, `APP_PASSWORD`) compared with `secrets.compare_digest`. No hardcoded secrets.\n- Unauthenticated requests redirect to `/login` (browser) or return 401 (API).\n- Upload page has **two sessions/sections**: Leave data and Onsite data. Each has year, month, and file input.\n\nYear/month inputs:\n\n- Year: integer (e.g. 2026)\n- Month: dropdown of January–December, stored as 1–12, converted to `september` for the object key\n\n## Storage behaviour\n\nMinIO/S3 has no real folders. The backend will:\n\n1. Build the prefix: `{dataset}/{year}/{month_name}/`\n2. List objects with that prefix\n3. If none exist, **create a folder marker** (`put_object` with key ending in `/`) so the month folder appears in the MinIO console before the file is written\n4. Upload the workbook to `{prefix}{safe_filename}`\n\nExamples:\n\n- Leave, Sept 2026 → `s3://lakehouse/leave_employee/2026/september/LeaveApplicationReport.xlsx`\n- Onsite, Sept 2026 → `s3://lakehouse/onsite_employee/2026/september/DailyAttendance_July.xlsx`\n\nFilename sanitization: keep the original name, strip path components, reject empty or non-`.xlsx` files. If an object with the same name already exists, overwrite it (ingest already overwrites Iceberg from all files in the folder).\n\nMinIO connection via env (same meaning as Airflow `GLOBALS`, not hardcoded):\n\n- `S3_ENDPOINT` (e.g. `http://minio:9000`)\n- `S3_ACCESS_KEY` / `S3_SECRET_KEY`\n- `S3_REGION`, `S3_BUCKET` (default `lakehouse`)\n- `S3_SECURE` (false to match current Spark `connection.ssl.enabled=false`)\n\nUse boto3 with path-style access, matching the Spark DAGs.\n\n## API surface\n\n| Method | Path | Purpose |\n|--------|------|---------|\n| GET | `/login` | Login form |\n| POST | `/login` | Authenticate, set session cookie |\n| POST | `/logout` | Clear session |\n| GET | `/` | Upload UI (auth required) |\n| POST | `/api/uploads/leave` | Multipart: `year`, `month`, `file` |\n| POST | `/api/uploads/onsite` | Same shape |\n\nResponse includes the created prefix and object key so the UI can show success.\n\nLight validation only: `.xlsx` extension and non-empty file. Header/schema checks stay in the Spark jobs so this service does not duplicate ingest logic.\n\n## Config and run\n\n- `pydantic-settings` + `.env` (gitignored). Ship `.env.example` with placeholder values.\n- `SESSION_SECRET` required for cookie signing.\n- Run locally: `uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8080`\n- Pin deps in `requirements.txt`: `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `python-multipart`, `jinja2`, `boto3`, `pydantic-settings`, `python-dotenv`, `itsdangerous`, `pytest`, `httpx`\n\n## Tests\n\n- Auth: unauthenticated upload → 401/redirect; wrong password rejected; valid login can upload\n- Path builder: month `9` → `september`; invalid month rejected\n- MinIO service (mocked boto3): missing prefix creates folder marker, then puts the object; existing prefix skips marker and only puts the file\n- Upload API: rejects non-xlsx; happy path returns the expected key\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Triggering `leave_data` / `onsite_employee` Airflow DAGs\n- Excel header parsing or Iceberg writes\n- Multi-user accounts / SSO\n- Dockerfile / K8s (can add later if needed)\n",

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Using Python 3.9+ union syntax `type | None` for type hints.

A redundant check in `sanitize_filename` is harmless. `create_s3_client` should use `Optional[Callable]` instead of `type | None` to avoid naming conflicts.

The S3 client factory will use `Optional[Callable[..., BaseClient]]`. Next comes the main application, templates, CSS, and README. For authentication, a simple dependency function checking `is_authenticated` is preferred over HTTPException redirects.

HTTPException 307 redirects may be wrapped as JSON by FastAPI. The upload page will handle redirects directly in its route handler. A separate API login dependency will handle authenticated endpoints.

API routes will raise HTTPException(401) for unauthenticated requests. HTML routes will handle redirects directly. The auth module will be simplified accordingly. The FastAPI upload endpoint is being defined.

The upload endpoint will accept year and month as form fields and require API login. Empty files will be rejected with a 400 error. The S3 client will be provided through a dependency. Session middleware is also being added.

SessionMiddleware will use the session secret from settings. A `create_app()` factory will initialize the FastAPI app and add middleware, since `get_settings()` reads environment variables at module load. Tests will clear the settings cache and rebuild the app. This factory will live in `main.py`.

Jinja2Templates will use a Path relative to the app directory. The UI will be a clean, professional design with simple typography and two cards. The login flow will have separate GET and POST handlers; authenticated users will be redirected away from the login page.

Login will use `secrets.compare_digest` for both username and password to prevent timing attacks. Invalid credentials will return a 401 response with an error message. This requires equal-length strings to avoid exceptions in some versions.

Year and month validation errors will return HTTP 422. Flash messages will be stored in the session and displayed on the upload page. HTML forms will post directly to the API endpoint, though non-JS clients may see raw JSON responses.

A helper function will manage upload responses. It stores flash messages in the session and redirects to the home page for HTML requests. JSON responses will be returned for API calls. Logout will be handled as a POST endpoint only. The implementation is now ready to be written.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
FastAPI TemplateResponse has changed its signature across newer versions. It now accepts either `TemplateResponse(request, name, context)` or `TemplateResponse(name, context)` with the request passed inside the context dictionary.

The older TemplateResponse signature is safer. It passes the request inside the context dictionary rather than as a separate argument.

The unused JSONResponse import will be removed. A module-level app instance in main.py causes test failures because environment variables are not yet set during import. Tests will configure environment variables in conftest.py before importing the app, use explicit settings via create_app(), and mock the S3 client.

Uvicorn requires the module-level app instance, so the factory cannot be deferred to import time. Tests will override get_settings and inject a fake S3 client. The upload handler calls create_s3_client directly, making mocking difficult without patching the function path.

Dependency injection will replace direct S3 client creation. A `get_s3_client` dependency will be injected into endpoints, allowing tests to override it cleanly. FastAPI Form fields for year and month will be coerced to integers automatically. The annotated `require_api_login` parameter is valid even though the dependency returns None.

HTML form uploads correctly trigger the wants_html check because the Accept header contains text/html. TestClient JSON requests correctly bypass HTML rendering since the Accept header is application/json.

Default TestClient sends `Accept: */*`, so JSON responses are returned automatically. Browser-style form uploads require `Accept: text/html` to trigger HTML redirects. Unused imports including `JSONResponse` and `month_label` will be removed from `main.py`. A `pytest.ini` or `conftest` will be added to configure test environment variables.

A FakeS3Client class is being defined for testing. It stores objects in memory and tracks put calls. It implements list_objects_v2 and put_object methods to mimic real S3 behavior.

Empty storage prefixes require a folder marker object before the actual file upload. Existing prefixes only need the file object.

The dataset field type mismatch will be handled with a type ignore or cast.

compare_digest safely handles credential comparison even when username lengths differ. The APP_USERNAME setting enforces a minimum length of one through Pydantic validation.

FastAPI documentation continues to show the older TemplateResponse signature with the request passed inside the context dictionary.

A pytest.ini with `pythonpath=.` will let tests import modules with `from app...` paths. The conftest will clear the settings cache before importing the app so tests can override environment variables. Unauthenticated HTML form uploads to `/api/uploads/leave` will receive a 401 JSON response. Unauthenticated GET requests to `/` will redirect to the login page. The next step is to update `main.py` and write the tests.

Dependencies will be installed and pytest will be run once the implementation is ready. The employee_ migration will be deferred until tests pass. FastAPI Form fields guarantee string inputs, so compare_digest is safe against non-string attackers. Python 3.12 allows compare_digest to handle differing username lengths. TemplateResponse and S3 dependency injection fixes are being applied.
</details></think>

_**Agent (grok-4.6)**_

The layout and FastAPI upload service are in place. Reopen Cursor at **`/Users/s.shameem/saal_employee`** — the old `/Users/s.shameem/employee_qa` path no longer exists.

```
/Users/s.shameem/saal_employee/
  employee_qa/              # moved as-is (employee_data + saal-data-model)
  employee_upload_api/      # new FastAPI project
```

**What the API does**
- Login page (username/password from env, session cookie)
- Two upload sessions: leave and onsite
- Year + month on each upload
- Stores `.xlsx` in MinIO `lakehouse` as `leave_employee/{year}/{month}/` or `onsite_employee/{year}/{month}/` (lowercase month names, e.g. `september`)
- Creates the month folder marker first if that prefix is missing
- Does not trigger Airflow DAGs

**How to run**
```bash
cd /Users/s.shameem/saal_employee/employee_upload_api
source .venv/bin/activate
cp .env.example .env   # set real credentials
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8080
```
Then open `http://127.0.0.1:8080`.

**Tests:** 18 passed (`pytest` in `employee_upload_api`).

**Not run:** live MinIO upload, browser UI against a real bucket. Fill `.env` with your MinIO endpoint and app login before using it.
